title: Merchandise Purchases — Counting Standing Days on Debit, Cash and Bank Card Purchases
content:
For a Price Accuracy Promise correction of a Merchandise Purchases unit, the standing days run from the purchase date to the request date and are counted by the tender shown on the purchase record:

- **Debit card or cash.** For a unit paid by debit card or cash, whose money left the customer's account on the purchase date, the standing days are the calendar days from the purchase date to the request date counting both dates.
- **Bank credit card.** For a unit paid by bank credit card, the standing days are the calendar days from the purchase date to the request date, not counting the purchase date.

A unit paid by any other tender (a Marlowe & Finch card, a gift card or mixed tender) is outside this rule.

## Worked counts (hypothetical dates: purchase 1 March, request 20 March)

| Tender on the purchase record | Count | Standing days |
|---|---|---|
| debit | 1 March through 20 March, both dates counted | 20 |
| cash | 1 March through 20 March, both dates counted | 20 |
| bank card | 2 March through 20 March | 19 |

A request on the purchase date itself gives 1 standing day for debit or cash and 0 for a bank card.
